# 7-day sample menu: in-center hemodialysis

--8<-- "includes/starting-points.md"

On hemodialysis protein goes **up**, to 70–84 g a day for 70 kg (1.0–1.2 g per kg), because dialysis removes protein and too little causes muscle loss. Potassium stays under 2,500 mg, phosphorus under 1,000 mg and sodium well under 2,000 mg, and fluid is counted: drinks plus foods that are liquid at room temperature (sherbet, gelatin, ice). The menus use about 450–850 mL of the 1,500 mL starting allowance, which leaves room for drinks with medicines and on hot days. Days 1, 3 and 5 are dialysis days (Monday, Wednesday, Friday). Saturday and Sunday fall in the long weekend gap, the riskiest time for high potassium and fluid overload, so those days stay at the low end.

## The numbers this menu is built to

Built for a reference adult: 70 kg, 170 cm, type 1 diabetes, using the app's starting targets for **Hemodialysis** (see [Eating well](../index.md#your-numbers)). Every day below was checked against these numbers by `scripts/build_handbook.py`.

| Per day | Built to |
|---|---|
| Protein | 70–84 g (1.0–1.2 g/kg) |
| Potassium | at most 2,500 mg |
| Phosphorus | at most 1,000 mg |
| Sodium | at most 2,000 mg |
| Fluid (drinks and foods that are liquid at room temperature) | at most 1,500 mL |
| Energy from food | 1,750–2,450 kcal |
| Carbohydrate | about 55 g at each main meal (every meal 50–60 g); snacks 10–30 g |

Also: no foods with phosphate additives.

## Swaps that keep the numbers

- **Egg whites** are the lowest-phosphorus protein: about 3.6 g protein for 5 mg phosphorus each.
- **Drinks:** water, tea or coffee can replace each other cup for cup; all of them count toward fluid, and so do ice chips, sherbet, gelatin and ice pops.
- **Protein foods:** chicken, turkey, pork loin, cod and pot roast swap ounce for ounce; salmon and tilapia have more potassium (about 330 mg per 3 oz).
- **Fruit and vegetables:** stay with the low-potassium list in ½-cup portions on non-dialysis days, especially on Sunday.

## Make it yours

- **Scale for your weight.** Protein here is 1.0–1.2 g per kg for 70 kg. At 60 kg that is 60–72 g a day, at 80 kg 80–96 g: change the meat at lunch and dinner by about ¾ oz for each 5 kg. Use the weight your unit gives you (often your dry weight).
- **Fluid is personal:** the 1,500 mL here assumes you still pass about 500 mL of urine a day. Your unit sets your allowance and checks it at every session.
- **Carbohydrate stays steady:** about the same amount at each main meal every day, so a fixed insulin plan or a carbohydrate ratio works the same way from day to day. Your own amount per meal comes from your diabetes team; keep it consistent and count what you actually eat ([Carb counting](../carb-counting.md)).
- **Lows on dialysis days:** glucose often drops during and after a session. Check before and after, carry glucose tablets (they add no fluid), and treat a low straight away ([Treating a low](../../t1d/treating-a-low.md)). Your team adjusts insulin for dialysis days.
- **Hungry, or losing weight without trying?** Add calories with olive oil, unsalted butter or more measured starch covered by your usual insulin plan, not with more meat, and tell your dietitian ([Eating enough](../eating-enough.md)).
- **Log it in the app:** every food here is in the app's food list under the same name. Saved meals and "copy day" let you reuse a menu day ([Planning and menus](../../app/planning-and-menus.md)).

## Sources

- [USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)][FDC]: every nutrient value, through the app's food list.
- [KDOQI 2020 nutrition guideline][Q20]: energy 25–35 kcal/kg (statement 3.1.1) and protein (statements 3.0.1–3.0.4).
- [KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline][K24]: sodium under 2 g a day (Rec 3.3.2.1); protein 0.8 g/kg at G3–G5 (Rec 3.3.1.1); limit bioavailable potassium only when it runs high (PP 3.11.5.2).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 11][A26-11]: protein 0.8 g/kg with diabetes and CKD before dialysis, 1.0–1.2 g/kg on dialysis (Rec 11.3).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 5][A26-5]: consistent carbohydrate in time and amount for people on fixed insulin plans (Rec 5.28).
- [NKF: carbohydrate counting with CKD][DG7]: 15 g is one carbohydrate choice; 3–6 choices per meal, set by your dietitian.
- [DaVita: hemodialysis fluid intake][DG23] and [AKF Kidney Kitchen: fluids][DG19a]: about 1,000 mL a day plus your urine output.
- [Foley 2011][DG53]: the long gap between sessions carries the highest risk; [Cabrera 2015][DG28a]: weight gain between sessions above 3.5 % of body weight is linked to death.
